content: Administer an initial test dose of 200 mg intravenously (IV), followed by 1 g IV on days 1, 3, 7, 14, and 21. Subsequently, administer 10 mg/kg IV every 5 days for a total of 12 injections. This regimen may be repeated after one month. Use this treatment in conjunction with tryparsamide. For the treatment of hormone-refractory prostate cancer, administer 20 mg/kg IV on days 1, 3, 7, 14, and 21, ensuring that no single dose exceeds 1 g. Reported adverse effects include vomiting, urticaria, paresthesia, peripheral neuropathy, kidney damage, blood dyscrasias, polyuria, polydipsia, pancytopenia, shock, optic atrophy, hypersensitivity reactions, proteinuria, and renal toxicity. Avoid use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Pregnancy Category: No human studies have been conducted to assess safety during pregnancy. Lactation: It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk. Absorption of the drug is poor, with a volume of distribution (Vd) of 90 ± 21 L during the terminal phase and 38 ± 8 L at steady state. The drug has a half-life of 36–60 days in the terminal phase. Peak plasma concentrations exceed 100 mcg/mL. The drug undergoes no metabolism and is excreted via urine. Adding plans allows for comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class.
